sections.name: normalizeUrl
sections.title: Making a link address complete
sections.what: Turns a typed address into a full link. It keeps full web addresses, adds https to bare domains and protocol-relative addresses, and keeps paths on this site. Empty input gives nothing back.
sections.why: Likely reason: users often type addresses without the https part, and uploaded report links point to this same app.
sections.watch_out: Text it does not recognize is treated as a domain name and gets https added, so this function does not check that a link is safe.

sections.name: buildJumpUrl
sections.title: Building a link to a page or passage
sections.what: Adds a jump target to a source address: a page number for PDFs, a named anchor, or a text highlight of up to 200 characters. With no locator, the excerpt alone becomes a text highlight.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets a citation open at the exact passage in the source document.
sections.watch_out: Excerpts are cut at 200 characters without regard to word or emoji boundaries, which can split a character and make encoding throw an error.

summary: Turns typed or stored addresses into full working links, and builds links that jump to a page or a passage.
purpose: Makes source and citation links open at the right place in the document.
why: The comments show it serves uploaded report links and document citations. The rest of the reason is implied rather than stated.
how: 1. Trims the address. 2. Adds https to bare domain names and protocol-relative addresses. 3. Keeps paths on this same site. 4. For a jump link, adds a page number, an anchor or a text highlight to the end of the address.
inputs: An address string, an optional locator (a type and a value), and optional excerpt text.
outputs: A full address string, or an empty string when no address is given.
risks: This is not a safety check: unrecognized text is treated as a domain and gets https added. Excerpts are cut at 200 characters, which can split a character and make encoding fail.
debug: If a link goes to the wrong site, check the stored address. If a jump link opens at the top, check the locator type and value. If building a link throws an error, check the excerpt for text that was split.
